title: Effects of Self-Efficacy-Oriented Art Therapy on Quality of Life in Adolescents and Young Adults Undergoing Medical Rehabilitation
summary: Adolescents and young adults with serious physical illnesses often experience emotional distress that can affect their quality of life. This study investigates whether a structured art therapy program, provided during inpatient medical rehabilitation, can improve well-being, confidence in dealing with everyday challenges, and overall quality of life. Participants receiving rehabilitation with or without art therapy will complete questionnaires at the beginning and end of their rehabilitation stay. In addition, a small number of participants will be invited to take part in voluntary interviews to better understand their personal experiences with art therapy. The findings will help to improve psychosocial rehabilitation programs for adolescents and young adults with chronic or serious illnesses.
conditions: Adolescents and young adults undergoing inpatient medical rehabilitation with or after cancer, cystic fibrosis, congenital or acquired heart diseases

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
inpatient medical rehabilitation at Nachsorgeklinik Tannheim, diagnosis of cancer, cystic fibrosis, congenital or acquired heart disease, chronic lung disease, inflammatory bowel disease, type 1 diabetes mellitus, or obesity, sufficient German language skills to understand the study information and complete the questionnaires, ability to complete the questionnaires independently, and written informed consent; for minors, additional written informed consent from a parent or legal guardian.
Exclusion criteria:
Failure to meet one or more inclusion criteria.
